title: GPU slice gateway and tenant quota sentinel
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Problem: Dedicated customers are experiencing unpredictable tail latency and throughput degradation when noisy tenants temporarily consume disproportionate GPU bandwidth. Current coarse hard-quotas and tenant lane reservation designs either underutilize fleet capacity or cause abrupt preemptions that break customer SLAs.

Goal: Implement a lightweight admission-and-control plane ("GPU Slice Gateway") plus a tenant quota sentinel service that enforces temporal throughput guarantees, provides graceful degradation, and drives autoscaling triggers with predictive noisy-neighbor suppression. The solution should prioritize tenant separation, minimize noisy neighbor impact, and allow transparent quota accounting for reporting and billing.

Scope: Implement control-plane components (gateway + sentinel), runtime enforcement hooks (cgroup/ML runtime pacing integration), telemetry & signals for noisy-neighbor detection, autoscale policy integration for Dedicated pools, and an operator playbook for escalations and rollbacks. This ticket covers the core gateway + sentinel MVP and integration tests; follow-ups will handle UI/console visibility and billing pipeline integration.
acceptance_criteria: GPU Slice Gateway accepts tenant allocation requests and returns slice tokens with stable capacity estimates (tokens include throughput window and priority metadata)
Quota Sentinel enforces a per-tenant sliding-window throughput token-bucket at the fleet-edge and can apply soft-rate-limits without immediate hard-preemption
Noisy-neighbor detector flags tenants with anomalous GPU memory/compute/PCIe utilization patterns with >85% precision on historical traces
Autoscale policy can be triggered by sentinel signals to provision burst capacity within committed latency (SLO: add capacity within 90s for P1 bursts)
Graceful fallback policy implemented: when quota is exceeded, requests either queue with backoff or fallback to a lower-cost model variant depending on tenant policy

End-to-end integration tests that simulate multi-tenant noisy bursts show capped impact: 95th percentile latency for protected tenants degrades by <=20% vs baseline and throughput for protected tenants remains >=90% of baseline under synthetic noisy burst
Telemetry surfaced to Console: per-tenant throughput, sentinel decisions, eviction counts, and autoscale events
Operators can manually invoke tenant soft-quiesce and have documented runbook for recovery
implementation_steps: Design and spec: converge on token format, admission flow, and sentinel decision thresholds (doc: Confluence/design/gpu-slice-gateway)
Proto: implement Gateway gRPC endpoint that issues time-bound slice tokens and records allocations to fleet ledger
Runtime hooks: add cgroup pacing shim to inference runtime to honor slice tokens (soft-rate limit path first)
Sentinel: implement sliding-window token-bucket evaluation and noisy-neighbor classifier using existing telemetry (prom/trace samples)
Autoscale integration: wire sentinel alerts to Dedicated autoscale controller with configurable escalation windows
Fallbacks: add model-variant routing in router to select degraded model pipeline when tenant is throttled
End-to-end tests: multi-tenant chaos tests using workload generator to verify degradation bounds
Observability: emit per-tenant metrics and traces; add Console dashboard mockups for PM/Design review
Security & compliance: threat model review and KMS signing for slice tokens
Rollout: gated canary behind feature flag; monitor key metrics and have automatic rollback on SLO breach
notes: Trade-offs: Soft-rate limiting preserves client requests and avoids hard preemption, but requires careful denial-of-service protections to prevent token forgery; we will sign tokens with KMS and verify at runtime.
Design choice: Use sliding-window token-bucket (per-tenant + per-lane) instead of global fair-queue to retain burst absorbency while bounding long-tail misuse.
Telemetry: leverage existing per-request kernel-level metrics (GPU sm utilization, PCIe stall counters, runtime queue length) and compute a lightweight anomaly score in Sentinel.
Prediction: a short ML classifier (lightweight XGBoost) on historical telemetry may reduce false positives; fallback to threshold-based rules for MVP.
Ops: add runbook for "soft quiesce" where tenant requests are routed to a holding queue and notified via webhook; escalation to CS for customer coordination.
Open question: exact SLA semantics when autoscale cannot provision extra capacity within escalation window (proposal: prioritized degrade based on customer tier and credit consumption).
Billing: current billing pipeline expects tokenized usage events; we will add sentinel-derived adjustment events for throttled requests in a follow-up ticket.
